about: The secreta of the formulary “Holy Thursday — Mass of the Lord’s Supper” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: May He Himself, we beseech You, O Lord, holy Father, almighty eternal God, render our sacrifice acceptable to You, He who by today’s institution showed His disciples that this was to be done in commemoration of Him, Jesus Christ, Your Son, our Lord, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God,

a.g: who lives and reigns with You

ex.w001: The Father is addressed as Lord, holy Father and almighty eternal God. “He Himself” is Christ, whose name comes later: Jesus Christ, Your Son, our Lord. The petition asks that Christ make our sacrifice acceptable to the Father. “We ask” is a parenthetic petition.
ex.w024: Christ showed His disciples that this was to be done in remembrance of Himself. “This” refers to the sacrificial action. The Latin delays “showed” until after “by today’s institution.” “His” and “Himself” refer to Christ, not to the Father. The wording recalls Christ’s institution of the Eucharist, not Judas’s betrayal.
